verdict: Neither curator nor background_review spawns a new OS-level forked/subprocess agent run, and neither opens an independent SessionDB writer handle against ~/.hermes/state.db. Both spawn an in-process daemon thread that runs a fresh AIAgent instance ('the fork') inside the SAME process, and both explicitly detach that fork from persistence (session_db defaults to/forced to None, _persist_disabled=True). So there is no parent/child writer-handle race via these two auto-trigger mechanisms as currently implemented; they are not the source of DeletedWalGenerationError.

findings.claim: Curator auto-trigger is idle-gated and runs via threading.Thread (in-process), not a subprocess/fork() of a new OS process.
findings.evidence: run_curator_review() starts threading.Thread(target=_llm_pass, daemon=True, name='curator-review').start() unless synchronous=True; maybe_run_curator() (the idle-triggered entrypoint) calls run_curator_review with default synchronous=False.

findings.claim: The curator's LLM review pass constructs a NEW AIAgent object ('review_agent') in the same Python process/thread, not a subprocess.
findings.evidence: from run_agent import AIAgent; review_agent = AIAgent(model=model_name, provider=provider, ..., enabled_toolsets=['skills'], max_iterations=9999, quiet_mode=True, platform='curator', skip_context_files=True, skip_memory=True) -- a plain Python object construction inside _run_llm_review(), called from the daemon thread.

findings.claim: The curator's forked AIAgent is never given a session_db, so it has no SessionDB handle at all (agent._session_db stays None by default) and therefore cannot write to state.db.
findings.evidence: AIAgent.__init__ signature defaults session_db=None; the curator's AIAgent(...) call in _run_llm_review() does not pass session_db, so agent_init.py sets agent._session_db = session_db i.e. None. No session_id is passed either, so no session row exists for it to write into.

findings.claim: Curator's idle-trigger entrypoint (maybe_run_curator) is called in-process from several call sites, none of which fork/exec a new process.
findings.evidence: Called from gateway/run.py _housekeeping_curator() (a scheduler-tick function), cli.py _tui_startup_background_maintenance(), and hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py serve-mode tick -- all direct Python function calls, not subprocess.Popen/os.fork/multiprocessing.

findings.claim: background_review's post-turn auto-spawn is also a daemon thread inside the same process, not a subprocess.
findings.evidence: spawn_background_review_thread() returns a _target closure passed to threading.Thread(...) by the caller (AIAgent.run_conversation); _run_review_in_thread runs _run_review_fork which builds build_cache_parity_fork(agent, ...) -> AIAgent(**_fork_init_kwargs(...)), a plain object construction.

findings.claim: background_review's forked AIAgent explicitly nulls its SessionDB handle and disables persistence, specifically to prevent it writing into the shared session store while sharing the parent's session_id.
findings.evidence: review_agent._skip_mcp_refresh = review_agent._persist_disabled = review_agent.suppress_status_output = True; review_agent._end_session_on_close = False; review_agent._session_db = None; review_agent.session_id = agent.session_id -- comment: 'PERSISTENCE ISOLATION (curator-takeover root cause): sharing the parent's session_id, the fork would otherwise write its harness turn into the REAL session'.

findings.claim: Usage/cost accounting for the background_review fork is deliberately routed through the PARENT's existing session_db handle only, never through a fork handle -- i.e. only the parent process ever writes for this feature, and only through its own already-owned handle.
findings.evidence: _record_review_usage_to_parent reads session_db = getattr(parent_agent, '_session_db', None) (the PARENT's handle) and calls session_db.record_auxiliary_usage(...); comment states 'The fork has _session_db = None so conversation_loop's DB-gated accounting never sees its calls'.

findings.claim: A defense-in-depth exists in the session-store layer for the failure mode this isolation prevents (harness text leaking into the real session), confirming the isolation is intentional and previously fixed, not incidental.
findings.evidence: _strip_background_review_harness / _is_background_review_harness_message in hermes_state.py strip any stray background-review harness turn on read, and a dedicated test module documents the original bug this isolation fixed.

findings.claim: The review_idle_queue (defer logic for the managed-local runtime) only delays WHEN the in-process thread is dispatched; dispatch is still the same in-process agent._spawn_background_review_now(**kwargs) call -- no subprocess is introduced by the idle-defer path either.
findings.evidence: item.agent._spawn_background_review_now(**item.kwargs) inside ReviewIdleQueue._run(), a plain method call on the already-live agent object from a dedicated bg-review-idle-queue daemon thread.

findings.claim: DeletedWalGenerationError and the state.db generation/identity guard machinery exist in hermes_state.py to detect a real out-of-band file replacement or an actually-competing writer handle -- a different (and real) hazard class than the curator/background_review fork mechanism, since these forks never acquire a handle at all.
findings.evidence: hermes_state.py tracks self._db_file_identity, self._retired_generation_capture, _STATE_DB_GENERATION_KEY in a state_meta table, and raises DeletedWalGenerationError/StateDbReplacedError when a handle's view of the db file's identity/generation no longer matches -- this guards against genuinely separate SessionDB() instances (e.g. multiple OS processes, or a stray CLI invocation) opening the same physical state.db file, not against these two auto-review threads which hold no handle at all.

recommended_action: Rule out curator.enabled and agent.auxiliary.background_review.enabled as the direct cause of the recurring DeletedWalGenerationError: as implemented, both auto-triggers run in-process (daemon threads, not forked OS processes) and their forked AIAgent instances are explicitly given no SessionDB handle (session_db=None / _persist_disabled=True), so they cannot race the parent gateway's writer. Redirect the incident investigation to (a) any separate OS-process invocation of `hermes curator run` or a foreground `/refine` CLI session running concurrently with the gateway against the same ~/.hermes/state.db (a genuinely separate SessionDB() instance with its own generation/application_id bookkeeping), (b) other cron jobs or multiplexed profiles/gateway instances pointed at the same state.db, or (c) a WAL-incompatible filesystem (NFS/SMB/FUSE) noted in hermes_state.py's own hint text. If curator/background_review are still suspected, add a regression test asserting review-fork agents always have `_session_db is None` (or `_persist_disabled is True`) at spawn time so this isolation cannot silently regress.
